_comment_warrens_anchor: AMBIGUITY: section D's RT-06 and section G both put the Warrens mouth at (-420,2470), which is data/config/map_landmarks.json's REGION centre. data/config/burrow_warrens.json's own `site.at` is (-357,2610), about 150 m away. Transcribed by walking the protocol's anchor first (where the GF-09-WARRENS-01 frame is taken, because that is the anchor section G names) and then on to the site the complex is actually built at.
_comment_interior: Section D describes RT-07 only as 'Warrens interior (entry -> guardian -> exit) | interior' -- it supplies no coordinates. The interior anchors below are derived from burrow_warrens.json's chamber offsets against `site.at` and are the transcriber's, not the protocol's.
_comment_evidence_lane: §H/§G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27, recorded in docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md §H.1. This is the LOGIC lane: the journey run headless for mechanics, telemetry and step verdicts at 6.1 ms/frame against 12,721 ms for a rendered frame on the Gate F container. It takes no prescribed frame; the §G ids its steps would have taken are DELEGATED to S06C, which declares each of them in its "owes" list. The harness refuses to start this segment if S06C does not exist, does not declare evidence_lane=capture, or does not accept every id handed to it -- a delegation nobody accepted is a debt that has quietly stopped existing, which is the same shape as the 9,231 file:null PASSes CD-1 was written for. Whether the debt was actually PAID is a question about the whole run directory and is answered by tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py, not here.
_comment_record_hz_split: AMENDED for the §H/§G evidence split. record_hz is forced to 0 on a logic lane by the harness regardless of what this file says, because §H's continuous record is the thing the split removes: the recorder's cadence is counted in PLAY seconds now, but under a 12.7 s rendered frame even a 0.1 Hz record fires on every rendered frame, and the eighteen segments' 4,607,802 physics frames are ~8,283 hours. The obligation is not dropped -- §H's prescribed frames move to S06C, which may run BOUNDED record windows around a named state.

args.text: Section B: this segment's entry save is `S05-exit`. The three steps below are the handoff's own mechanics: the live save directory is emptied first so the title's Load list has exactly one non-empty slot and auto-focuses it (`title_screen.gd` focuses the FIRST non-empty slot), then slot 4 is seeded from the run directory, then the load is driven through the production title-screen Load path by synthetic input. Section B names the seed and the Load path; the wipe is not named there and is recorded here as an added mechanical step, needed because an autosave left in slot 0 would take the auto-focus and the segment would load the wrong state.

args.text: Section H: 'Mandatory for the highest-risk segments: ... every band handoff +/-60 s (region transitions)'. steps.title: Section L.3 band 2 crafting: the protocol names no site, but the world authored one

args.text: Section L.3 requires 'S06 orb_greater + reinforced tools -- each paid at real cost'. Section B's S06 span does not mention crafting and the protocol names no crafting site in band 2, so the workbench below is placed by the player at the quarry, where the tier material is. RECORDED as the transcriber's siting of a requirement section L.3 states and section B's span omits. CL-H8 VERDICT, 2026-09-04, decided by one live probe (tools/_probe_workbench_context.gd) rather than by argument: the workbench beat below (S06-31..S06-49) SHOULD BE REMOVED, and it is NOT masking a game defect. The reason it was in doubt: S06's own run recorded `build_catalogue` never releasing input after a workbench interact, and S08 hit the same stuck context by a different route, so the beat might have been the only thing photographing a real shared-UI bug in build_menu.gd / craft_panel.gd / game_menu.gd. It is not. Driven through the real nodes in a live world and read through the harness's own resolver (scripts/debug/gate_f_probe.gd::input_context), the whole sequence is clean: world -> open the catalogue -> build_catalogue -> close it -> world -> place a real workbench through build_placer.gd -> world -> interact its CraftInteractable -> panel:<craft_panel.gd>, NOT build_catalogue -> cancel -> world. The interact does not even enter the catalogue context; it opens the craft panel, and every context releases. So S06's stuck catalogue belongs to CL-H13 (the harness input path resolving against a context the action does not belong to, seen at three independent sites) and not to the workbench, and removing this beat hides nothing. WHAT W20 DID AND DID NOT DO, and what closed it: W20 edited only this step, because S06-31..S06-49 were another lane's territory, and handed the deletion on with the verdict (ralph/reports/W20-SMALL-FIXES-0904/REPORT.md). N10-HARNESS-TESTS-0905 carried it out. S06-31..S06-49 are DELETED and section L.3's crafting requirement is rehomed to band 2's own authored crafting site -- the `ranger_camp` cluster's `craft_at` anvil -- in steps S06-30a..S06-30l immediately below, which is exactly the home this note said the requirement needed and could not find. The claim in this step's title that band 2 'has no authored crafting site' is what changed: it was true of the protocol's own text and is not true of the shipped world, where scripts/world/rest_point.gd stands a real CraftInteractable at every authored camp that carries one.

steps.title: CL-H8: the invented workbench beat is gone; L.3 moves to band 2's authored anvil

args.text: CL-H8 CLOSED, N10-HARNESS-TESTS-0905. Steps S06-31..S06-49 stood here: open the pause shell, cycle to Build, arm a Workbench, PLACE it at the player's feet in the Old Quarry, interact it, craft, close. They are gone. They were a transcriber's invention, and W20-SMALL-FIXES-0904 proved it by live probe rather than by argument (tools/_probe_workbench_context.gd, driving the real nodes and reading the harness's own resolver): world -> open the catalogue -> build_catalogue -> close it -> world -> place a real workbench through build_placer.gd -> world -> interact its CraftInteractable -> panel:craft_panel.gd -> cancel -> world. The workbench interact never enters build_catalogue at all, so the 'stuck catalogue' this beat was scripted around is not a game defect this beat was photographing; it belongs to CL-H13, the harness's own input path resolving against a context the action does not belong to. Removing the beat hides nothing. WHAT REPLACES IT, because section L.3's requirement ('S06 orb_greater + reinforced tools -- each paid at real cost') is real and survives the deletion: band 2 DOES have an authored crafting site, which is what S06-30's own note said this beat needed and could not find. data/config/bands/band2_stone_and_root/props.json's `ranger_camp` cluster carries a `rest` block with `craft_at: [-259.6, 2257.4]` and `craft_label: "Craft at the ranger's anvil"`, stood up as a real CraftInteractable by scripts/world/rest_point.gd (T5-CADENCE; tests/smoke_authored_camps.gd already asserts that an authored camp offers craft as well as rest). The camp is on the `ranger_camp_spur` loop between the quarry and the Warrens mouth and is a named map landmark (`band2_ranger_camp`, 'Abandoned Ranger Camp'). So the crafting is done where the game authored a place to do it, on rootstone the player broke out at the quarry one step earlier, instead of at a workbench conjured on the spot.

steps.observation: N10-HARNESS-TESTS-0905. MEASURED, not routed: a single straight `move_to` from the quarry at (403, 1794) to the ranger camp does NOT go. Run today on this branch it burned all 30,000 walking frames with 0 held and stopped 734.2 m short at (340.0, 4.0, 1834.0), and the route trace shows why: 544 play-seconds inside a 78 m x 66 m band with `dead_travel_m` climbing to 1,986 m. That is W21-HARNESS-FIGHTS-0904's S06-50 signature at the same place (it logged 711 s and 1,258 m of dead travel at (336.2, 1.3, 1820.6), 14 m from where this stopped) -- and it settles that lane's own hypothesis: the pin is NOT the just-placed workbench confusing navigator state. There is no workbench any more; this branch deleted S06-38 with the rest of the invented beat, and the body still cannot leave the quarry on that bearing. It is the Old Quarry's own exit. THE FIX IS THE AUTHORED ROUTE, not a bigger budget: `data/config/terrain_playground.json`'s `trail.bands[band2_stone_and_root]` spine runs (400,1800) -> (330,1950) -> (180,2050) -> (20,2130) -> (-150,2210) -> (-310,2320) -> (-420,2470), and the ranger camp sits on the `ranger_camp_spur` loop that leaves that spine at (-150,2210) and rejoins it at (-310,2320). These legs walk it. Nothing teleports and no terrain moved.
